{"standalone":"How does receivables advance (antecipação) work with Getnet?","search_queries":["antecipação de recebíveis como funciona"],"intent":"knowledge","plan":["faq"],"language":"en","confidence":0.9}

input.query: How does receivables advance (antecipação de recebíveis) work with Getnet?
antecipação de vendas Getnet como solicitar taxa

content.text:
Antecipação lets you receive your card sales before the normal settlement date. You can do it in the Getnet Brasil app, which has no extra fee [6].

- **Timing:** A sales schedule can be advanced from D+1 (one business day after the sale) until D-3 (three business days before settlement) [8].
- **Consent:** Getnet needs your authorization to look up your schedule at the Registradora (the receivables registry) [7]. You aren't charged more than the existing fees, such as rental, MDR and the advance fee [7].
- **Card brands:** Sales from some card brands can't be advanced through Getnet, only with the brand's own operator [8].
- **Automatic advance:** For the "Receba Conforme suas Vendas" plan, Antecipação Automática is a condition for the exemption. Getnet assesses each contract individually, because it is a credit approval [3].
- **Gravame:** If you use your receivables as collateral for a loan, they are directed to the lender. With Getnet, your sales are paid into your Get Conta up to the loan's outstanding balance [1][2].
- **E-commerce:** Advances on e-commerce sales are blocked for 6 months [5].

The sources don't give a specific advance fee percentage. The tax table I found shows other rates, such as an additional monthly rate of 2.73% on the 2-business-day plan, but it doesn't call this the advance fee [10].

- **Card brands:** Sales from some card brands can't be advanced through Getnet. Those need the brand's own operator [sup-antecipacao-de-vendas-10].
